I started Kidney Watch to keep myself up to date. Kidney transplantation moves quickly, and staying current is a job that never quite finishes. What you see below is the first pass I built for my own reading — made public because what helps me keep up is, I suspect, useful to other clinicians trying to do the same.

Every week, [Claude](https://claude.ai) searches PubMed for kidney transplantation research from the previous 14 days and shortlists up to eight papers — the trials, registry and cohort studies, guideline updates, and reviews I judge most worth a UK transplant clinician's time. Each gets a plain-language summary, and every citation is checked against PubMed before I review the issue and publish it.

It is a deliberately small, curated first pass — not a complete index, and not a substitute for reading the primary sources. Always verify against the original publication before relying on anything here.

Curious how it runs unattended? I wrote up the whole pipeline — the weekly schedule, the citation-verification step, and what keeps AI-generated clinical content safe to publish — in [From a literature-search skill to a self-running evidence digest](/posts/automated-literature-watch/).

**Found this useful?** Leave a comment below — here for general feedback, or under any individual issue. You can follow new issues via the [RSS feed](/briefings.xml) now, with an email subscription to come. And if you'd like a digest tuned to your own sub-specialty or search query, [register your interest](mailto:laszlo.szabo@wales.nhs.uk?subject=Personalised%20transplant%20briefing).
